docs.title: SCD2 Timeline Anatomy
docs.text: Understanding how Slowly Changing Dimension Type 2 tracks history over time.

docs.title: What is SCD2?
docs.text:
SCD Type 2 creates a new row for every change to tracked attributes, preserving complete history.

Example: Customer "Alice" changes her address twice.

docs.title: Timeline Visualization
docs.text:
gantt
    title Customer #101 (Alice) - Address History
    dateFormat YYYY-MM-DD
    section Portland
    Version 1 (SK=1001)     :active, v1, 2024-01-01, 2024-06-15
    section Seattle
    Version 2 (SK=1002)     :active, v2, 2024-06-15, 2025-01-10
    section Boston
    Version 3 (SK=1003)     :active, v3, 2025-01-10, 2099-12-31

docs.title: Initial Load (2024-01-01)
docs.text:
Customer moves to Portland.

customer_sk customer_id name city is_current valid_from valid_to is_deleted 1001 101 Alice Portland TRUE 2024-01-01 9999-12-31 FALSE

Explanation: - customer_sk = 1001 → Surrogate key (unique, never reused) - customer_id = 101 → Natural key (from source system) - is_current = TRUE → This is the active version - valid_to = 9999-12-31 → No end date yet (current record)

docs.title: First Change (2024-06-15)
docs.text:
Customer moves to Seattle.

graph LR
    A[Source: Alice<br/>city = Seattle] -->|Merge| B{Match on<br/>customer_id?}
    B -->|Yes| C{City changed?}
    C -->|Yes| D[Close old row<br/>Open new row]
    D --> E[SK=1001<br/>is_current=FALSE<br/>valid_to=2024-06-14]
    D --> F[SK=1002<br/>is_current=TRUE<br/>valid_from=2024-06-15]

Result:

customer_sk customer_id name city is_current valid_from valid_to is_deleted 1001 101 Alice Portland FALSE 2024-01-01 2024-06-14 FALSE 1002 101 Alice Seattle TRUE 2024-06-15 9999-12-31 FALSE

Key Changes: - Row 1 (SK=1001): is_current → FALSE, valid_to → 2024-06-14 - Row 2 (SK=1002): New row with Seattle, is_current → TRUE

docs.title: Second Change (2025-01-10)
docs.text:
Customer moves to Boston.

customer_sk customer_id name city is_current valid_from valid_to is_deleted 1001 101 Alice Portland FALSE 2024-01-01 2024-06-14 FALSE 1002 101 Alice Seattle FALSE 2024-06-15 2025-01-09 FALSE 1003 101 Alice Boston TRUE 2025-01-10 9999-12-31 FALSE

Now we have 3 versions of customer 101, each with its own surrogate key.

docs.title: SCD2 State Diagram
docs.text:
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Current: New record inserted
    Current --> Historical: Attribute changes
    Historical --> [*]: Retention policy

    Current: is_current = TRUE<br/>valid_to = 9999-12-31
    Historical: is_current = FALSE<br/>valid_to = change_date

docs.title: Tracked vs Non-Tracked Columns
docs.text:
Not all columns need history tracking. Choose wisely.

Column Type Track Changes? Example Tracked ✅ Yes (creates new version) address, email, tier, status Non-Tracked ❌ No (update in place) phone, last_login, preferences Fixed 🔒 Never changes customer_id, signup_date, birth_date

Example YAML:

pattern:
  type: dimension
  params:
    natural_key: customer_id
    surrogate_key: customer_sk
    scd_type: 2
    track_cols: [name, email, city, tier]  # Only these trigger new versions

docs.title: Get Current State
docs.text:
SELECT *
FROM dim_customer
WHERE is_current = TRUE;

Returns 1 row per customer (latest version).

docs.title: Get Historical State (Point-in-Time)
docs.text:
"What was Alice's address on 2024-10-01?"

SELECT *
FROM dim_customer
WHERE customer_id = 101
  AND valid_from <= '2024-10-01'
  AND valid_to >= '2024-10-01';

Returns: | customer_sk | customer_id | name | city | valid_from | valid_to | |-------------|-------------|------|------|------------|----------| | 1002 | 101 | Alice | Seattle | 2024-06-15 | 2025-01-09 |

docs.title: Get Full History
docs.text:
SELECT customer_id, city, valid_from, valid_to, is_current
FROM dim_customer
WHERE customer_id = 101
ORDER BY valid_from;

Returns: | customer_id | city | valid_from | valid_to | is_current | |-------------|------|------------|----------|------------| | 101 | Portland | 2024-01-01 | 2024-06-14 | FALSE | | 101 | Seattle | 2024-06-15 | 2025-01-09 | FALSE | | 101 | Boston | 2025-01-10 | 9999-12-31 | TRUE |

docs.title: Delete Detection
docs.text:
If a customer is deleted from source:

customer_sk customer_id name city is_current is_deleted 1003 101 Alice Boston FALSE TRUE 
pattern:
  type: dimension
  params:
    detect_deletes: true
    deleted_flag_col: is_deleted

docs.title: Unknown Member (SK=0)
docs.text:
For orphan fact records (customer not in dimension):

customer_sk customer_id name city is_current 0 NULL Unknown Unknown TRUE 
pattern:
  type: dimension
  params:
    unknown_member: true  # Creates SK=0 row

Fact records reference SK=0 when customer_id is missing.

docs.title: SCD2 vs SCD1
docs.text:
Feature SCD1 (Overwrite) SCD2 (Versioned) History ❌ No ✅ Yes Storage Small Large Queries Simple Moderate Use Case Latest state only Audit, compliance, trends

When to use SCD2: - Compliance requirements (GDPR, SOX) - Trend analysis (how has customer tier changed?) - Slowly changing attributes (address, status)

When to use SCD1: - Non-critical attributes (preferences, UI settings) - High-frequency changes (no value in history) - Storage constraints

docs.title: Odibi SCD2 Example
docs.text:
nodes:
  - name: dim_customer
    read:
      connection: bronze
      table: raw_customers

    pattern:
      type: dimension
      params:
        natural_key: customer_id
        surrogate_key: customer_sk
        scd_type: 2
        track_cols: [name, email, city, tier]
        effective_from_col: valid_from
        effective_to_col: valid_to
        current_flag_col: is_current
        deleted_flag_col: is_deleted
        detect_deletes: true
        unknown_member: true

    write:
      connection: silver
      format: delta
      table: dim_customer
      mode: overwrite

First run: Inserts all customers with is_current = TRUE Second run: Detects changes, closes old rows, opens new rows Third run: Detects deletes, sets is_deleted = TRUE

docs.title: ❌ Wrong: No Surrogate Keys
docs.text:
# BAD: Using natural key in fact table
fact_orders:
  customer_id: 101  # ❌ Which version of customer?

docs.title: ✅ Right: Use Surrogate Keys
docs.text:
# GOOD: Using surrogate key
fact_orders:
  customer_sk: 1002  # ✅ Exact version (Seattle address)

docs.title: ❌ Wrong: Tracking Too Many Columns
docs.text:
# BAD: Tracking high-frequency changes
track_cols: [name, email, city, tier, last_login, page_views]
# Creates new version on every login!

docs.title: ✅ Right: Track Only Business-Critical Changes
docs.text:
# GOOD: Only track meaningful changes
track_cols: [name, email, city, tier]

docs.title: ❌ Wrong: No Unknown Member
docs.text: Facts referencing SK=NULL break BI tools.

docs.title: ✅ Right: Unknown Member Handling
docs.text:
params:
  unknown_member: true  # Creates SK=0 for orphans
